newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate debt market - feast or famine.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate debt market - feast or famine.

text.p: Investor appetite for new corporate debt amid a shortage of supply caused players to scramble for leftovers in the secondary market on Friday, dealers said.
"There's a lot of demand and not a whole lot of paper ... there's definitely a lot of cash out there," said one syndicate source.
Another syndicate source echoed this view. "Deals this week were all priced attractively and later traded at a tighter spread in the secondary market."
While investors anxiously search for more supply to devour, a number of deals are currently being worked.

Among next week's offerings expected to be snatched up by investors are US West Inc unit, US West Capital Funding Inc's $2.0 billion four-part offering, which is rumored will be upped in size. The deal is expected to be underwritten by Merrill Lynch.
"Talk in the market is that the deal may now come in between $2.0 and $3.0 billion," one high-grade syndicate source said.

Currently, price talk on the five-year issue is seen between 55 and 60 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries. The 10-year issue is seen between 80 and 85 basis points, and the 30-year is seen at 110 basis points.
Price talk on the 40-year tranche is seen between 55 and 60 basis points. The issue is puttable in the seventh year.
The following deals were among this week's successful debt offerings.
Polaroid Corp's $300 million two-part debt offering via lead manager Lehman Brothers met good demand and was boosted in size from an initial $250 million.
Merrill Lynch & Co Inc's Aa3/AA-minus 7.25 percent 10-year debt offering was upped in size to $500 million from an initial $350 million.
Lehman's $300 million Baa1/A-rated 10-year notes were increased from an initial $200 million.
Tosco Corp's $600 million Baa2/BBB-minus rated multi-tranche debt offering via Morgan Stanley was also priced very successfully with all issues tightening in the secondary market.
Dealers said they expected activity to pick up next week as the search for corporate paper continues.
